definition: Limited Memory AI is a type of artificial intelligence that uses past data and experiences for a short period of time to make decisions or predictions.
details: Unlike reactive AI systems, which respond only to current inputs, limited memory AI can temporarily store information and learn from recent observations. Most modern artificial intelligence systems are considered limited memory AI.

explainer.lead: Limited Memory AI is a type of artificial intelligence that uses past data and experiences for a short period to make decisions or predictions. It matters because most modern AI systems fall into this category, unlike reactive systems that only respond to current inputs.

tiers.eli5: It's like a driver who remembers the last few minutes of the road to steer better, but doesn't recall yesterday's trip.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers design systems that temporarily store recent observations to inform decisions, but must manage the memory window carefully; a pitfall is that too long a memory can slow responses or include outdated information.
tiers.paperLevel: Limited Memory AI temporarily stores information and learns from recent observations, distinguishing it from reactive AI; its known limit is that the memory is short-term, so it cannot leverage long-term historical patterns.

explainer.example: A self-driving car that remembers the positions of nearby vehicles from the last few seconds to predict their next moves is using limited memory AI.
